artifact: PART B evidence — rps/rkill on live Houdini 22.0.368
producer: Live GUI Houdini session over the SYNAPSE WS bridge (protocol 4.0.0), hou.isUIAvailable()=True, main thread. Every row below is a verbatim capture, not a summary.

controls.why: Law 1 — a probe that cannot demonstrate success against a known-good target produces uninterpretable failures.
controls.scene_positive_control: Before concluding anything about background renders, a FOREGROUND mantra render of the same scene was proven to write a real EXR (49,863 bytes with renderTime metadata). This ruled out 'my scene is broken' as the explanation for an empty rps.
controls.result: controls green in every capture below.

commands_exist.rps: EXISTS. help: 'Lists background render processes. The command lists the PID of the process, the host which the command is running on, the command being run, and the frame being rendered.'
commands_exist.rkill: EXISTS. help: 'Stop or pause/unpause a render. USAGE rkill [-s | -r] <process_pattern>'. Examples include 'rkill *  Kills all render processes'.
commands_exist.hou.RopNode_cancel_verb: ABSENT — re-confirmed this leg. dir(hou.RopNode) render-ish names: addRenderEventCallback, cook, render, removeRenderEventCallback, removeAllRenderEventCallbacks, _cookNoInterruptInternal. No cancel/abort/interrupt/stop/kill.

F1_rkill_is_silent.claim: rkill reports NOTHING on either success or no-match, so it cannot be its own receipt.
F1_rkill_is_silent.evidence_success: hou.hscript('rkill 72712') -> out='', err='' — and the process was in fact killed (tasklist confirmed dead).
F1_rkill_is_silent.consequence: server/render_stop.py verifies every stop by re-reading rps. Law 3.

F2_dead_rows.claim: rps retains COMPLETED renders as rows with PID -1. They are not killable.
F2_dead_rows.evidence: PID Command / -1 mantra x7 accumulated across the session's finished renders.

F3_mapping_husk_MAPPABLE.claim: usdrender_rop (Karma/husk) renders ARE attributable to their ROP.
F3_mapping_husk_MAPPABLE.mechanism: rps reports husk's full command line, which contains a per-invocation temp scene at usd_renders/usdrender_<houdiniPID>_<node.sessionId()>_<counter>/__render__.usd

F4_mapping_mantra_NOT_MAPPABLE.claim: ifd/mantra renders CANNOT be attributed to a ROP by any available field.
F4_mapping_mantra_NOT_MAPPABLE.evidence_rps: Two concurrent mantra renders: 'PID Command / 31416 mantra / 75828 mantra' — the Command column is the bare word 'mantra' for both.
F4_mapping_mantra_NOT_MAPPABLE.evidence_os: Win32_Process CommandLine for both PIDs is literally 'mantra' with no arguments — Houdini pipes the IFD over stdin (soho_pipecmd='mantra'), so the OS command line is bare too.
F4_mapping_mantra_NOT_MAPPABLE.consequence: render_stop returns status='unmappable' and REFUSES rather than killing the only render running. Verified live: stop_render(node_path='/out/h3b_mantra') -> 'unmappable', killed=False, while stop_render(pid=10272) -> 'stopped', killed=True.

F5_rkill_is_pid_selective.claim: rkill <pid> kills ONLY that process; other renders survive.
F5_rkill_is_pid_selective.method: Two concurrent husk renders from two different ROPs, one killed by its mapped PID.

evidence.watch_5s: B_alive False at t=0.5s and every sample after; A_alive TRUE at every sample through t=5.0s

F5_rkill_is_pid_selective.false_start_recorded: An EARLIER run of this test showed both renders gone after the kill and looked like proof that rkill is not selective. It was re-run rather than reported: A had simply finished naturally (it had been running far longer). The corrected run above is the evidence. Recorded because the wrong version was one report away from shipping.

F6_partial_frame_MANTRA_hazardous.claim: A stopped mantra render leaves a STRUCTURALLY VALID but PIXEL-EMPTY EXR at the real output path.
F6_partial_frame_MANTRA_hazardous.killed_file_is_valid: iinfo -v exits 0 and reports Resolution 1920x1080, full header, correct EXR magic 762f3101. It PARSES. It has no pixels.
F6_partial_frame_MANTRA_hazardous.why_this_is_the_dangerous_case: It is not corrupt — it is valid-and-empty, so any 'does the file exist and parse?' check passes it.
detectors: orphaned <output>.mantra_checkpoint beside the frame (removed on clean completion)
EXR header lacks renderTime / renderMemory / date — a completed mantra frame carries all three (observed: renderTime=3.157328, renderTime_s='0:00:03.16')

F7_partial_frame_HUSK_safe.claim: A stopped Karma/husk render CANNOT corrupt the declared output — it simply never appears.
F7_partial_frame_HUSK_safe.mechanism: husk writes progressive snapshots to a SEPARATE file <stem>_part.exr and writes the declared output path only on completion, removing _part as it goes. The usdrender_rop invokes it with --snapshot 300.
F7_partial_frame_HUSK_safe.after_completion: h3b_snap.exr present (2,378,855 bytes); h3b_snap_part.exr ABSENT — removed on completion.
F7_partial_frame_HUSK_safe.after_kill_mid_render: Killed husk (rop B) produced NO file at its declared output path at all.
F7_partial_frame_HUSK_safe.temp_dirs: usdrender_<pid>_<sid>_<n>/ temp dirs were cleaned up even for the killed render. One stale dir from 2026-07-24 (usdrender_73500_82_1) exists but predates this run and is not attributable to rkill.

F8_scope_not_covered.foreground_renders: A foreground/in-process render never becomes a background process, never appears in rps, and cannot be reached by rkill. Measured: with soho_foreground=0 a mantra render() returns in 0.054s (spooled); the render itself runs in a separate mantra.exe.
F8_scope_not_covered.IPR: hou.IPRViewer.killRender EXISTS and is a DIFFERENT case — interactive preview, not a ROP render. Not wrapped by this leg. Noted and left there per brief PART B.4.
F8_scope_not_covered.rkill_wildcard: 'rkill *' kills every background render on the host including renders this session never started. Deliberately unreachable from render_stop.
